content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":4,"description_fidelity":5,"readability_1x":5,"pixel_craft":6,"palette_discipline":9,"appeal":6},"score":57,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["At 1x the diagonal silhouette reads more like a tiny rocket, drill, or comet than a floating squid.","The face lacks two clearly separated eyes, so the red-warning behavior has no obvious visual anchor.","The long upper black stalk feels like an antenna and weakens the squid-like mantle silhouette.","The lower-left appendages merge into one narrow, noisy mass instead of reading as tentacles gathering for a thrust.","The outline varies from one to several pixels thick around the right and lower body, unlike the controlled Capcom contouring of MM2/MM3.","Large white and cyan interior shapes form awkward stair-steps and make the body look hollow rather than mechanically constructed.","The sprite is taller than the intended compact 16-20 px footprint and has weak visual balance around its diagonal axis."],"fixes":["Compress the silhouette into a roughly 18x18 body-and-tentacle footprint.","Remove or shorten the top stalk and shape the upper body as a broad, rounded squid mantle with small side fins.","Place two distinct 1-2 px eyes across the front of the body; reserve a red alternate-frame color for the warning flash.","Separate the lower appendage into three bold tentacles with clean 2-3 px-wide clusters and two animation poses: gathered and thrust outward.","Reduce the heavy right-side and underside black masses to a mostly 1 px contour, using thicker black only at deliberate shadow joins.","Replace the checker-like white/cyan interior with one simple white face plane and one cyan shadow band.","Keep the strong black, cyan, and white palette, but arrange each color into larger, cleaner NES-style clusters."]}
